title: Grafted groups of neural crest cells keep their identity; single grafted cells do not

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Grafted groups of neural crest cells keep their identity; single grafted cells do not

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Single neural crest cells transposed to a different anterior-posterior axial domain change their gene expression to match their neighbours, whereas groups of transposed cells keep their original gene expression, which the authors interpret as collectives having greater positional memory (a perceptual field extending further into the past) than individual cells.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › Neural crest intelligence is collective

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Individual cells transposed from one anterior-posterior axial domain to another will change their gene expression to match their neighbors159,161,162. In contrast, groups of cells transposed along the anterior-posterior axis maintain their original gene expression, thus resisting the inductive effects of the surrounding tissue159,161,162.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: McMillen P, Levin M, “Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates”, Communications biology (2024), doi:10.1038/s42003-024-06037-4; section “Introduction › Neural crest intelligence is collective”. Scope: Vertebrate neural crest (chick, mouse) transplantation

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-collective-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Donor-versus-host expression is a direct, discriminating outcome and the single/group contrast is experimentally clear. Existing reports can establish the contrast, while positional-memory language and alternative group-protection mechanisms remain only partially resolved.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify axial identity-marker expression after transplanting single cells or size-matched groups and compare retention of donor identity with neighboring host identity over time.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Historical graft studies may not expose cell-level raw data.

Group grafts differ from single cells in survival, microenvironment, and inductive exposure.

analysis feasibility: 0.7
data existence: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Donor versus host Hox expression after single-cell versus group grafts is a defined contrast, and the mouse transposition paper publishes it with lineage labels. Related chick and zebrafish grafts are separate papers, not a combined open count matrix. The expression difference can be re-examined from those figures for a few vertebrates, while the memory and perceptual-field gloss is not an additional variable in the data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare Hox or reporter expression of single neural-crest or rhombomere cells grafted to a new axial level with expression of coherent groups grafted to the same level. Groups keeping donor expression while isolated cells matching the host would support the contrast; both classes changing, or both keeping donor identity, would refute it. A longer 'perceptual field' is not a further measurement beyond that retention.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Graft size, dispersion and cell survival are entangled in the classic experiments.

Maintained gene expression does not measure memory duration or a perceptual field extending into the past.

Counts are in figures from mouse, chick and zebrafish papers, not one deposited cell table.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.48
operationalizability: 0.8
analysis feasibility: 0.34
